title: Core growth between the #59 reference (9a835cc) and the v1 freeze, recorded for the owner's decision
proposedAddition: No new addition: this records growth that already happened on the capability-parity branch before Core was frozen, so that the approved baseline in architecture/core-baseline.json does not silently absorb it. Measured by npm run check:core-budget: handwritten Core went from 3 files / 675 raw lines / 435 code lines (src/protocol.ts, src/kernel/browser-kernel.ts, src/kernel/diagnostics.ts) to 7 files / 1341 raw / 922 code lines, adding src/guest/handshake.ts, src/kernel/binding-policy.ts, src/kernel/capabilities.ts and src/kernel/handshake.ts; generated Core went from none to src/generated/core.ts and core.codec.ts (1031 lines); emitted Core gzip from 7112 to 23540 bytes. Root exports stayed at 59, now all Core (the 35 federation and reference-engine names left the root in #61) in six families instead of five: optional-capability-seam is the new family. Concepts (7), binding primitives (6), built-in families (4) and runtime dependencies (0) did not change.
invariantOrUseCase: Each growth serves an existing Core concept rather than adding one. correlation-compatibility: one language-neutral contract with a fingerprint handshake (#52), so F#, C#, Rust and TypeScript engines and the kernel refuse to run on a mismatch instead of misreading each other. typed-capabilities: the generic optional-capability seam (#16), which is what lets every new browser capability ship as an optional pack instead of a fifth built-in family. projection-output: the binding security policy (#18: unsafe URL schemes, forbidden attributes and elements) and head binding (#38). typed-capabilities: protocol 1.2-1.4 Http and form-control semantics (#47), including OutcomeUnknown{connection-lost} for unsafe methods.
whyNotHtmlCss: None of it is presentation or structure: the handshake, the seam, and URL safety are enforced where the engine's messages are applied, which HTML and CSS cannot see.
whyNotEngineLibrary: An engine library runs inside one engine and cannot make the host refuse an incompatible engine, validate a projection, or route a capability result; each of these is enforced on the host side of the boundary for every engine language.
whyNotCapabilityPack: The seam is what packs plug into, so it cannot itself be a pack. The binding policy guards the six primitives, which are Core. The handshake must run before any pack is negotiated. The Http changes are to the grandfathered Http family's own outcomes.
whyNotForma: Forma owns interaction and presentation primitives; none of this is interaction or presentation. (Forma's content was not consulted from this repository: access was not granted to this session.)
whyNotGovernedAdapter: A governed adapter wraps a third-party surface with no application authority; these mechanisms are what adapters are themselves constrained by.
whyNotTooling: Tooling runs in development and CI; these run in every production page load.
whyNotHostRenderer: Every host (page, worker, server renderer) needs the same handshake, seam and binding rules; placing them in one host would make the others diverge.

consumerEvidence.consumer: Minimal F#, C# and Rust WebAssembly engines
consumerEvidence.evidence: guests/minimal/: each completes the fingerprint handshake and drives every built-in capability in Chromium (npm run smoke:guests)

consumerEvidence.consumer: The product site's F# WebAssembly engine

consumerEvidence.evidence: src/capabilities/*: every pack reaches engines only through the generic Capability seam in src/kernel/capabilities.ts

complexityDelta: Reference -> approved (npm run check:core-budget prints the full table): handwritten files 3 -> 7; handwritten code lines 435 -> 922 (+112%); raw lines 675 -> 1341 (+99%); handwritten normalized bytes 20320 -> 46922; generated lines 0 -> 843 code / 1031 raw; emitted gzip 7112 -> 23540 (+231%); root exports 59 -> 59 (families 5 -> 6, and 35 non-Core names removed); binding primitives 6 -> 6; built-in families 4 -> 4; runtime dependencies 0 -> 0; concepts 7 -> 7; minimal consumer gzip 12235 -> 23819 bytes.
compatibilityImpact: Protocol revisions 1.1-1.4 are additive and negotiated through the handshake: an engine at an older minor keeps the older behavior (e.g. timeout-after-dispatch instead of connection-lost). The root entrypoint's removal of federation and the reference engine (#61) is the one breaking change, documented in docs/18-naming-and-compatibility.md.
negativeBoundaryTests: test/core-boundary.test.ts (Core importing federation, a pack, the reference engine, a host, a renderer or tooling fails; a new Core file fails; a seventh primitive, a fifth family, a runtime dependency, an unapproved root export and an eighth concept fail); test/root-surface.test.ts (the minimal consumer loads Core only); test/core-budget.test.ts (every hard gate and 10% trigger has a failing fixture).
guestLanguageImpact: The contract is generated for F#, C# and Rust from contract/core.contract.json (npm run contract:check); each guest binding recomputes the fingerprint and runs the shared vectors (npm run test:guests). Rejecting this growth would mean removing the handshake or the seam, which every guest binding and minimal engine depends on.
